title: The queen out early
line: An early queen can make threats, but every attack on her brings out one of your pieces.

steps.text: White starts with the king pawn.
Push your king pawn two squares too. It takes your share of the center.
steps.after: White brings the queen out at once, as some players do. She attacks the pawn on e5 and looks at f7.

steps.text: Guard the pawn on e5 and bring a piece out at the same time.

also.d7d6: That guards the pawn too. This lesson brings a knight out.

steps.text: Now the queen and bishop both aim at f7. White threatens to take it with checkmate.
Block the queen's line with the pawn on g7. It attacks the queen as well.

wrong.g8f6: That attacks the queen, but it leaves f7. The queen takes it with checkmate.

also.d8e7: That guards f7 too. This lesson blocks with the pawn.

steps.after: The queen steps back but still aims at f7.

steps.text: Block her again, this time with a knight that comes out.
Bring the bishop out to g7, where the pawn move made room.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It opens the way for your other bishop.

also.e8g8: Castling is also sound here. This lesson opens the bishop first.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out with an attack on the queen.
steps.after: The queen moves a third time. Your pieces came out while she was chased.

summary: An early queen makes threats. Block them with pieces you need to bring out anyway, and chase her when you can.
